facts: Pan-tilt-zoom (PTZ) cameras have the capacity to simultaneously cover a panoramic area.
Pan-tilt-zoom (PTZ) cameras have the capacity to maintain high resolution imagery.
Researches in automated surveillance systems with multiple PTZ cameras have become increasingly important.
Most existing algorithms require the prior knowledge of intrinsic parameters of the PTZ camera to infer the relative positioning and orientation among multiple PTZ cameras.
A novel mapping algorithm is proposed.
The novel mapping algorithm derives the relative positioning between two PTZ cameras.
The novel mapping algorithm derives the relative orientation between two PTZ cameras.
The novel mapping algorithm is based on a unified polynomial model.
Dependence on the knowledge of intrinsic parameters of PTZ camera is reduced.
Dependence on relative positions is reduced.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm presents substantially reduced computational complexity, as compared with the work of Chen and Wang.
Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm presents improved flexibility, as compared with the work of Chen and Wang.
The proposed algorithm has slightly decreased pixel accuracy.
The slightly decreased pixel accuracy can be compensated by consistent labeling approaches.

The compensation of slightly decreased pixel accuracy occurs without added cost for the application of automated surveillance systems along with changing configurations and a larger number of PTZ cameras.
